textures.prompt:
Create one original square, full-bleed seamless 2D albedo texture tile for Gredice, a sunny toy-diorama garden game. Straight-on orthographic material swatch filling the entire image. Use clean, simple hand-painted shapes with few color values and smoothly feathered transitions. Keep color variation extremely low in contrast, within 15% of the base brightness, and evenly distributed without a focal spot. This will display at 200 pixels wide. Use flat even illumination across the tile. Opposite edges must continue naturally into each other on both axes with no framing or symmetry. No gradient across the whole tile, vignette, cast shadow, photographic texture, stipple, flecks, noise, outlines, text or watermark. Output exactly one tile, with no samples, separators or margins.

Subject is top-down, very closely mown lawn, average sRGB #7bd03a. Almost uniform fresh yellow-green, with an exceptionally quiet wash of large, soft brush patches in slightly warmer yellow-green and cooler green. Blend their edges until the shapes are nearly imperceptible. Keep the patches distributed and free from striping. The effect is barely richer than solid color. Use nothing but those soft painted patches: no literal blades, V shapes, tufts, flowers, soil or bright strokes.
textures.processing: Converted the 1254 × 1254 source to sRGB and resampled it to 640 × 640. Matched and smoothly crossfaded 58px horizontal and 58px vertical overlaps for continuous wrapping. Downsampled with wrap-aware Lanczos to 512 × 512 and shifted the tile origin. Softened fine detail with a 8px wrapped Gaussian and reduced tile-wide color drift. Scaled painted color variation to 0.8× and used a soft luminance limit at ±4.5% of the target. Centered the mean sRGB values on #7bd03a and adjusted for the decoded color. Exported WebP at quality 92 with an embedded sRGB profile and reviewed a 3 × 3 repeat at 200px per tile.

textures.prompt: Create one original square, full-bleed 2D seamless albedo tile for cool grey-blue stone in a sunny toy-diorama game. Average sRGB #b3bdd3. Show only a flat stone material, straight on, filling all corners. Paint broad, sparse irregular interlocking facets in near-identical blue-grey colors, with smooth muted transitions and an even overall value. Two very short narrow hairline fractures are an important detail: each should be a slender dark blue-grey kink, at most a few pixels thick at game resolution, about 5–9% of tile width, lightly feathered but discernible in the source. One can follow the edge of a facet. Keep the two cracks unconnected and similar in prominence, with little contrast and no shadows. Soft hand-painted cut shapes, a touch of facet variation, clearly reads as a clean toy rock material. Everything else is quiet and flat. Seamless continuation left to right and top to bottom. No photograph, grit, spots, noise, margins, lighting direction, glints, gradients across the whole tile, border, text or watermark.

Scaled painted color variation to 0.82× and used a soft luminance limit at ±9% of the target. Centered the mean sRGB values on #b3bdd3 and adjusted for the decoded color. Exported WebP at quality 92 with an embedded sRGB profile and reviewed a 3 × 3 repeat at 200px per tile. Used a lighter softening pass to preserve the two short painted cracks.
